# API Rate Limits and Quota Management

This reference covers per-API rate limits, pagination best practices, and
backoff strategies for read-only Google Workspace API operations.

## Per-API Read Request Limits

| API | Per project (reads/min) | Per user per project (reads/min) | Source |
|-----|------------------------|----------------------------------|--------|
| Calendar | Not published | Not published | [13] |
| Drive | 12,000 / 60s | 12,000 / 60s | [14] |
| Sheets | 300 / min | 60 / min | [15] |
| Meet | 6,000 / min | 600 / min | [16] |
| Docs | 3,000 / min | 300 / min | [17] |

Notes:
- Calendar API does not publish numeric limits — only visible in Cloud Console [13]
- Drive quotas are stated per 60 seconds rather than per minute [14]
- All usage is free across all APIs; exceeding quotas incurs no charges [13][14][15][16][17]
- No daily request limits exist if per-minute quotas are respected [14][15]

## Quota Structure

Two dimensions enforced across all APIs [13]:

1. **Per-minute per project**: total requests from all users of your Cloud project
2. **Per-minute per project per user**: requests from a single user within your project

### Service Account Quota Attribution

When using domain-wide delegation, the service account (not the impersonated user)
is charged against per-user quotas by default [13]. To distribute load:
- Use the `quotaUser` URL parameter, or
- Set the `x-goog-quota-user` HTTP header

### Sliding Window

Calendar API (and likely others) uses a rolling minute window. Burst traffic
exceeding the per-minute quota causes rate limiting in the next window to
maintain average usage within quotas [13].

## Pagination Best Practices

### AIP-158 Standard [18]

Google's internal pagination standard:

| Rule | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Token opacity | Tokens are opaque URL-safe strings; base-64 encoding is NOT sufficient obfuscation [18] |
| pageSize | Optional; 0 or absent means API chooses default; values above max are coerced down; negative values → INVALID_ARGUMENT [18] |
| Token expiration | ~3 days practical rule of thumb (not documented) [18] |
| Parameter consistency | All parameters except pageSize must match between page requests [18] |
| End of collection | Empty/omitted nextPageToken is the ONLY signal for end of results [18] |
| Result count | APIs may return fewer results than pageSize, even mid-collection [18] |

### Per-API Pagination Defaults

| API | Default pageSize | Max pageSize | Notes |
|-----|-----------------|-------------|-------|
| Calendar events.list | 250 | 2,500 | [13] |
| Meet conferenceRecords | 25 | 100 | [16] |
| Sheets | N/A | N/A | Batch requests count as single call [15] |

### Pagination Safety for Automation

- **Do not change parameters between pages** (except pageSize) — this triggers
  INVALID_ARGUMENT [18]
- **Handle token expiration** — tokens expire after ~3 days; long-running jobs
  may need to restart pagination [18]
- **Use --page-all with caution** — the gws CLI's `--page-all` flag auto-paginates
  but produces NDJSON output (one JSON object per line), requiring merge logic
- **Respect fewer-than-requested results** — do not assume empty page means end;
  only empty nextPageToken signals completion [18]

## Exponential Backoff

All Google Workspace APIs recommend the same formula [14][15][16][17][19]:

```
wait = min((2^n + random_milliseconds), maximum_backoff)
```

Where:
- `n` starts at 0 and increments per retry
- `random_milliseconds` is 0-1000ms (prevents thundering herd) [19]
- `maximum_backoff` is typically 32-64 seconds [19]

### Reference Implementations

| Platform | Max retries | Initial delay | Multiplier | Max delay |
|----------|-------------|---------------|------------|-----------|
| gcloud CLI | 32 | 1s | 2x | 32s | [19] |
| Go library | — | 1s | 2.0 | 30s | [19] |
| Java library | 6 attempts | 1s | 2.0 | 32s | [19] |

### What to Retry

| Status code | Retry? | Reason |
|-------------|--------|--------|
| 408 | Yes | Request timeout [19] |
| 429 | Yes | Rate limit exceeded [19] |
| 5xx | Yes | Server error [19] |
| 403 rateLimitExceeded | Yes | Functionally identical to 429 [20] |
| Other 4xx | No | Client error (permanent) [19] |

### Anti-Patterns [19]

- Retrying without backoff delays
- Retrying non-idempotent operations unconditionally
- Retrying permanent client errors
- No maximum retry count
- Layering multiple retry mechanisms (e.g., application + library both retry)

## Quota Monitoring

- **Cloud Console**: IAM & Admin > Quotas & System Limits
- **APIs & Services Dashboard**: per-API traffic charts with response code breakdown
- **Cloud Monitoring**: Metrics Explorer for deeper analysis and custom alerting

## Gaps and Limitations

- Calendar API does not publish numeric quota values [13]
- Sheets API quotas (300/min project, 60/min user) appear lower than other
  APIs — may be a bottleneck for automation
- Whether batch requests count as 1 or N quota units varies by API (Sheets: 1 [15])
- The gws CLI does not expose quota monitoring or backoff configuration
